Consumer career guidance and financial planning benchmarks

  • Calibration and verification before shipping a money view

Research date: October 18, 2026. Audience: a high-school student and parent using a short, friendly career-exploration app.

The most useful combination is a short interest-led start, optional work-values refinement, understandable reasons for several career suggestions, and a separate local money scenario. None of the reviewed public evidence justifies treating a proprietary match score as the probability that a teenager will succeed in a career. The money view should compare clearly labeled wage distributions with an editable budget, then connect the student to education, training and financial-aid next steps.

Evidence and access boundaries

  • Documented means official vendor, government, institution or research documentation read through public web retrieval. Vendor claims remain attributed claims. Published time estimates are not measured completion times.
  • Observed is limited to Princeton Review's anonymous browser start screen: the visible session displayed the legacy 24-question form and its first four questions without sign-in. No answers were submitted. Other products were reviewed through public pages, FAQ text and sample reports; their complete flows and paid results were not tested.
  • No accounts, purchases, real student answers or financial details were supplied. No private data or school license codes were used. Publicly available price text establishes advertised pricing, not a completed checkout price.
  • MyPlan's canonical pages repeatedly timed out in direct web retrieval. Its official indexed pages supplied the quoted counts, timings and prices; the values page also appeared on an institutional MyPlan subdomain. Current operation of those assessments is unverified. College Scorecard and College Navigator landing pages also failed direct retrieval; their official documentation, rather than an invented live walkthrough, supports the comparisons below.

What the evidence supports about matching

PathwayU provides the strongest publicly explained research chain in this subset, but the distinction between construct validity, an intervention outcome and the accuracy of a particular ranked recommendation still matters. Its report discusses meta-analyses and an earlier-software randomized study involving over 600 students; outcomes were confidence, decision difficulty and related career-development measures. A benefit from software plus a 90-minute workshop does not demonstrate that a 20-minute current assessment can forecast an individual teenager's earnings or job satisfaction. PathwayU science report.

CareerExplorer's machine-learning/large-response-count claims and CareerFitter's calculation counts describe their methods or scale, not a published error rate. CareerFitter is unusually explicit about its unavailable technical statistics. For this app, use “suggested paths to explore,” a few response-based reasons, and room for disagreement. An 87% match should never be presented as an 87% chance of success without an actual probability target and out-of-sample calibration. These are interpretation and design conclusions drawn from the limits of the reviewed evidence. CareerExplorer explanation, CareerFitter limitations.

Avoid turning preference descriptions into fixed ability judgments. MyPlan explicitly distinguishes its skills self-assessment from aptitude; Truity's sample uses categorical strengths/challenges language and advises avoiding some tasks. A high-school student may have had little exposure to those tasks. Better follow-up: “Try a small project or talk with someone in this job,” then update the exploration list. MyPlan skills definition, Truity sample.

Money and education references

ReferenceBest role in this appDefinitions and limits that must travel with the number
BLS Occupational Outlook HandbookA readable career card: work tasks, work environment, how to enter, pay and projected outlook. Filters include entry-level education, on-the-job training and median pay.“Entry-level education” is a preparation descriptor; it does not make the separate median-pay field a starting salary. Outlook is a projection, not an individual's hiring probability. OOH, BLS explanation of OOH.
BLS OEWSDetailed occupational wage distributions for relevant geographies; pair the median with available 25th–75th percentiles and source year. Use an Austin metro estimate when available, with explicit state/national fallback.Median is the midpoint across wage/salary workers in an occupation. OEWS excludes self-employed workers and nonwage benefits; straight-time wages exclude overtime premiums and stock bonuses. Published annual estimates generally assume 2,080 hours. Thus, wage percentiles must not be relabeled as fixed years-of-experience milestones or total compensation. OEWS FAQ, tables, Austin official release index.
MIT Living Wage Calculator / Living Wage InstituteA transparent basic-needs baseline, by geography and household type, against which a chosen lifestyle can be compared. Method combines costs, taxes and working adults, assuming full-time 2,080-hour work.Model estimates, not observed household bills. Twelve family types; eight needs; 2026 inputs adjusted to December 2025 dollars. Baseline excludes restaurant dining, vacations and savings/retirement. Costs and taxes have different sources/assumptions; do not call the baseline a comfortable lifestyle. Methodology and technical report.
College ScorecardCompare institution or field-of-study costs, debt and reported earnings with careful cohort labels, then link to the source rather than promise personal ROI.Official technical documentation restricts earnings to federal-aid recipients and distinguishes institution cohorts from field-of-study completers. Early-career observation is not lifetime earnings; selection, further study, suppressed cells and cohort timing matter. Do not mix “years after entry” and “years after completion.” Documentation dates reviewed: institution June 2024, field of study April 2025; live latest-release status unverified. Institution documentation, field-of-study documentation.
NCES College Navigator / IPEDSFind actual institutions/programs and award levels; compare institutional cost, financial aid and completion context, with a route beyond bachelor's degrees.Historical aggregate net price is not a household-specific award. IPEDS cost-of-attendance budgets include tuition/fees, books/supplies, room/board and other expenses. Relevant cohort and year must remain attached. Direct current UI was not verified here. Official College Navigator, IPEDS cost reporting, NCES net-price definition.
College net-price calculatorsThe concrete next step after choosing two or three schools: personalized cost/aid estimate based on family inputs. Keep sensitive household questions outside the initial career quiz.Net price = cost of attendance minus grants/scholarships; loans are financing. UT Austin's current page describes a 2026–27 calculator and warns estimates use prior-year costs/aid, are nonbinding and are not actual awards. It states calculator data will not be shared or used for another purpose. UT Austin calculator explanation.
Federal Student AidExplain aid types, compare actual offers, link to early aid estimation and FAFSA when the family is ready.Its aid-offer guide separates grants/scholarships from loans and work-study and recommends comparing net price. The Federal Student Aid Estimator provides an early estimate of federal aid for college or career school, not an admission or final award decision. Avoid hardcoding changing annual aid limits into career results. Aid-offer comparison, estimator.

Texas Reality Check assumptions worth teaching explicitly

The FAQ says apartment rent uses HUD fair-market rents; home payments use area median sale prices, a 30-year mortgage and 20% down; insurance assumes a healthy adult in their twenties; student debt uses average yearly borrowing, with 20-year repayment for most degrees and 30 years for professional degrees. Those are modeling choices, not personal quotes or necessarily the student's actual loan terms. The FAQ's family-cost explanation uses USDA child-cost estimates. Texas Reality Check FAQ.

Transfer the approachable spending-choice interaction, but expose consequential assumptions beside the result. A small monthly debt payment created by a long repayment term can conceal higher lifetime interest. A home-payment scenario can conceal a large up-front down payment. Verify current sources and dates before reusing any default; the reviewed FAQ says “current” without giving a date for each input. A 2024 TWC budget request proposes user-entered expenses, Spanish and a self-sufficiency wage, but a proposal is not evidence those features shipped. FAQ, TWC request, page 6.

Austin examples and local next steps

  • Travis County baseline: use the same household and price year when comparing its basic-needs model with a chosen lifestyle. Exact current figures and licensing constraints are verified in the financial-methods addendum; the occupational table is not detailed county-career pay. County calculator.
  • Austin wage geography: the official BLS Austin index currently links an August 2026 release covering May 2025 OEWS data. Preserve observation year separately from publication/access date and the Austin–Round Rock–San Marcos metro boundary separately from Travis County. BLS Austin index.
  • Texas education routes: THECB offers a state net-price-calculator listing; ACC's 2026–27 catalog points families to it. TWC's State Training Inventory searches providers/programs by region, ZIP and field, covering public, private and proprietary providers. Availability is not proof of program quality or individual eligibility. THECB, ACC catalog, TWC training inventory.
  • Exploration without another survey: Workforce Solutions Capital Area connects school-age exploration to Climb the Ladder CTX and offers apprenticeship/training routes. Youth services have age and eligibility conditions; do not imply all students automatically receive funded training. A next-action link can connect a student to a local conversation or experience. Youth services, career/training/apprenticeship entry.

Transferable product ideas

The following are design recommendations derived from the comparisons, not claims that a short custom quiz has been validated.

  1. Start with one short module and an honest progress count. Aim for a friendly initial session around 5–10 minutes, subject to actual student testing. Show useful suggestions before offering optional values/preferences refinement. Do not require MyPlan's full four-test burden or CareerExplorer's longer full profile to see a first result.
  2. Explain several paths, including trades. Show a small set of varied options with “why this appeared,” a task the student might enjoy, a possible friction point and a short experiment. Use separate education-route cards for certificate, apprenticeship, associate and bachelor's pathways where appropriate; confirm each real path from its provider.
  3. Make financial fit a second lens. Keep personal interest and affordability visible separately. A student's desired spending should not silently rewrite their interests. Let them compare “this career with a smaller budget” and “this budget with other careers.” Texas Reality Check provides the useful two-way concept.
  4. Use an editable monthly scenario. Begin with location, living arrangement and household size, then housing, transport and discretionary choices. Expand details only when requested. Show gross wage → modeled taxes/deductions → take-home → expenses → savings/debt → remaining margin. Separate recurring costs from deposits, down payments and training costs.
  5. Preserve financial definitions. On salary cards show occupation, geography, year, median and available wage distribution. Label any lower-wage scenario as a scenario; a percentile is not a starting-pay claim. Do not derive a five-year salary trajectory from cross-sectional wage percentiles. Identify modeled taxes, hours, benefits, aid and loan terms explicitly.
  6. Show tradeoffs before precision. Round monthly results to useful amounts and show lower/base/higher scenarios or a sensitivity slider. Explain when rent, hours, household size or debt changes the conclusion. Do not invent statistical confidence intervals from a budget range. Missing data should produce “not available” plus a broader-geography fallback label.
  7. End with three concrete actions. Save two careers to compare, try one relevant experience, and check two education routes using their actual costs/net-price calculators. An optional parent discussion view should invite reflection; it should not turn a student's profile into a fixed label.
  8. Keep privacy and paywalls clear before effort. Truity's no-email basic-result approach is worth adapting; disclose what remains free at the beginning, not after dozens of answers. Make save/share optional and explain who can see a minor's results. Public privacy statements were not technically audited here; no vendor should be labeled “privacy safe” solely from them.

Calibration and verification before shipping a money view

For a product implementation, keep the exact public-data vintage and geographic key on every input, and save the household/scenario assumptions with the result. Validate calculations against a small set of official reference examples and independent recomputation; do not use competitors' attractive output as ground truth. Test zero/part-time hours, missing wages, roommates, multiple earners, no children, tuition versus total attendance cost, aid versus loans, and overlapping child/housing/medical categories. A baseline imported from MIT or Texas Reality Check must not be added to a second set of the same expenses.

Use a loan's actual principal, rate and term for the displayed scenario, with both monthly payment and total repayment. Keep college-study years and post-training work years separate and do not subtract tuition again from a wage that is already being shown after a loan payment. Label an assumed wage or inflation path as an assumption. Test these distinctions with students and parents: can they explain what the number includes and change one choice to improve the outcome? That is a more meaningful usability target than making the dashboard display an exact-looking dollar amount.

Unresolved commercial/research details requiring vendor documentation rather than inference: current PathwayU item counts and individual pricing; all proprietary scoring equations and teen-specific prospective calibration; Truity's current consumer checkout price; CareerExplorer's legacy membership discrepancy; MyPlan's live compatibility and source vintages; Princeton Review's rollout/version behavior and final result gate; Texas Reality Check's current tax/debt/cost vintage and completed-flow behavior. No ranking of actual predictive accuracy is justified by this public review.
